title: Introduce FlashPatch attention kernel with fused rope rewrite and KV prefetch optimizer
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Adds a new low-latency attention kernel (FlashPatch) with fused rope/rotary rewrite and KV prefetching. Improves throughput and p99 tail latency for medium/long-context workloads. Backwards compatible; opt-in behind kernel selector flag.
description:
Motivation: We have multiple production signals where mid-length chat workloads and long-prefix contexts suffer from KV-cache warmup and rotary/rope rewrite overhead (expensive rematerialization in the hot path). This PR introduces a new attention codepath, FlashPatch, which combines a low-latency FlashAttention-like kernel with a fused rope/rotary rewrite stage and an adaptive KV prefetch ring. The goal is to reduce p99 latency and improve steady-state throughput without changing model weights or API surface.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds flashpatch kernel implemented with a streamlined memory layout to reduce copies and shared-memory pressure.
- Integrates a fused "rope rewrite" step: rotary embeddings are applied in-kernel where possible, and when not possible we emit a lightweight staged rewrite that avoids full rematerialization.
- Implements a KV prefetch ring buffer that warms hot KV lanes predicted by the continuous-batcher's hinting API (scheduler improvements included).
- Extends the kernel_selector with a cost model that picks FlashPatch for latency-sensitive sequences and falls back to existing flashbridge/flashattn variants for other shapes.
- Adds unit and integration tests, microbench harness, and operator docs + a short rollout guide.

Benchmarks summary (see perf_summary field for numbers). Benchmarks were run on p4d-style instances and internal 8xA100 cluster; workloads include concurrency=8 autoregressive tokens with context lengths 1k/2k/8k. Microbench harness attached.

Compatibility and rollout: FlashPatch is behind a runtime feature flag (kernel_selector.flag=flashpatch). No model changes required. Default remains the current stable kernel; we will canary FlashPatch in dedicated clusters and gradually roll to Hosted with automatic fallback on elevated error/latency.

Checklist: 
- [x] Kernel implementation and CUDA micro-optimizations
- [x] Kernel selector integration and cost model
- [x] KV prefetch ring and scheduler hint plumbing
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Benchmark and ops rollout docs

Related work: touches the same subsystem as recent FlashBridge and FlashMosaic efforts (see ENG-2107, ENG-2198). This PR is intentionally a compact, opt-in path that targets a different tradeoff (latency-first with lightweight prefetch) than prior throughput-focused kernels.

perf_summary: Context length 1024, concurrency 8: +18% throughput (tokens/s) vs flashing-bridge baseline, p99 -9%
Context length 8192, concurrency 4: +6% throughput, p99 -4% (prefetch helps steady-state)
KV warmup: cold->steady latency drop reduced from ~2.1s to ~0.9s in synthetic long-prefix replay tests
CPU overhead: kernel selection adds ~0.5% CPU time in the request path (measured)
ci_checks: unit-tests: pass (GPU emu + small host suite)
lint: fail (minor clang-format issues) - fixed in followup commit
perf-regression: pass (no regressions on baseline models)
review_comments: Liam Chen: Great direction — please add a short note in the kernel_selector docs explaining the cost thresholds and stability expectations. Also ensure there is a guard for older GPUs lacking async copy semantics.
Priya Desai: Reply: added docs and backward guard (kernel falls back if async copy not supported). See kernel_selector.cpp lines referenced in commit d4e5f6a.
Marta Ivanov: Request changes: the prefetch ring currently grabs per-request affinity unconditionally; make it opt-in via continuous-batcher hints to avoid noisy prefetch under high churn.
Priya Desai: Reply: updated continuous_batcher to honor hints and added a flag to cap prefetch window. Benchmarks re-run and numbers updated.
Diego Alvarez: Approve with comment: consider adding a small telemetry counter for failed prefetches so we can tune thresholds in prod.
rollout_plan: Canary 1: enable FlashPatch on 5% of dedicated clusters (latency and error SLO monitoring) for 48 hours
Canary 2: enable on 25% of dedicated clusters with automatic fallback policy for 7 days
Hosted: enable behind a customer opt-in flag and collect telemetry for 14 days
Full: enable kernel selector default if no regressions detected after 30d
notes: This PR purposefully avoids changing public SDK APIs; exposure is a runtime configuration flag documented in docs/ops/rollout_flashpatch.md.
Follow-up work planned: 1) quantized kernel path for int8 support, 2) tighter integration with the hybrid-batcher cost model, 3) ops dashboard for prefetch heuristics.
Ops contact: @priay for canary and rollback instructions
